La tarea nos llevó 45 minutos, y aunque nadie se quemó, sí que se derramó algo de aceite. That night, Pablo dreamt he was getting lost on unknown streets, a nightmare that prompted him to act. The next day, with a blank map, he went out to explore; every discovery was an achievement. He spelt the name of the local bakery to memorize it and, upon arriving home, he told me how he suddenly jumped for joy when he found a small 2nd-hand bookstore. Later, while we were celebrating with coffee, he accidentally burnt a little of the cake I had prepared and told me, "Now I understand the importance of knowing every corner." Thus, Pablo learnt to master his new environment and I learnt a valuable lesson.

text_es: Dominar la técnica de aprender a silbar, ya sea con los labios o con los dedos, es un proceso que requiere paciencia y práctica. Recuerdo una tarde cuando mi hermano 1.º, empeñado en sorprender a mi padre, se apoyó en la encimera de la cocina mientras intentaba un silbido de 2 dedos. Quemó su dedo con la tostadora que acababa de usar, y del susto, derramó el zumo que tenía preparado. Aquella noche soñó que era un director de orquesta y que la melodía se estropeó porque no podía silbar. Al día siguiente, con la frente arrugada, deletreó lentamente «sil-bar» y aprendió una nueva técnica que finalmente le permitió emitir un sonido. Desde entonces, cada vez que lo oigo, me acuerdo de aquel desastre en la cocina.

text_nat: Mastering the technique of learning to whistle, whether with lips or fingers, is a process that requires patience and practice. I remember one afternoon when my 1st brother, determined to surprise my father, leaned on the kitchen counter while trying a 2-finger whistle. He burned his finger on the toaster he had just used, and from the fright, spilled the juice he had prepared. That night he dreamed he was an orchestra conductor and that the melody was spoiled because he couldn't whistle. The next day, with a wrinkled brow, he slowly spelled out "whis-tle" and learned a new technique that finally allowed him to make a sound. Since then, every time I hear him, I remember that disaster in the kitchen.

text_es: Para aprender a silbar, la paciencia es clave; recuerdo cuando mi primo, con solo 8 años, se propuso dominarlo. Empezó intentando diferentes formas con los labios, y a veces se frustraba. Una noche, mientras cocinábamos, se apoyó en la encimera y, distraído, no vio que la sartén estaba muy caliente y se quemó un dedo levemente, lo que lo hizo saltar del susto. Poco después, en su empeño por concentrarse, deletreó en voz alta la palabra «silbar» varias veces, como si eso ayudara. Al día siguiente me contó que soñó que silbaba una melodía perfecta. Poco a poco, con constancia, lo logró; aunque una vez, intentando celebrar un pequeño avance, derramó un vaso de agua y el libro de cocina se estropeó un poco. Su éxito fue una prueba de que la perseverancia da sus frutos.

text_nat: To learn to whistle, patience is key; I remember when my cousin, at only 8 years old, set out to master it. He started by trying different shapes with his lips, and sometimes he would get frustrated. One night, while we were cooking, he leaned on the counter and, distracted, didn't see that the pan was very hot and slightly burned a finger, which made him jump from fright. Soon after, in his effort to concentrate, he spelled out the word "whistle" several times, as if that would help. The next day he told me he dreamed he was whistling a perfect melody. Little by little, with perseverance, he achieved it; although once, trying to celebrate a small advance, he spilled a glass of water and the cookbook got a little spoiled. His success was proof that perseverance pays off.
